description: I’m participating in this challenge as a solo participant and I’m not looking for team members. I enjoy working with data and turning it into clear, practical insights, and I plan to use NASA’s open Earth observation data to build a simple solution with real-world impact.
summary: Harvest Compass is a free, multilingual decision-support tool that helps farmers anywhere in the world choose better crop rotations as weather shifts. A farmer enters their location, current crops, soil, water supply and priorities. Only then does the tool use NASA climate data to suggest which crops to sow when, compare possible rotations on water use, soil health, income and weather risk, and explain each result in plain language. It addresses the Field Shift challenge by turning NASA POWER, GPM IMERG and GLDAS data into clear, local guidance for hotter seasons and uneven rain. It matters because water, soil and income are at stake in every planting decision. It works in any country and supports 100 interface languages.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Harvest Compass recommends crop rotations for a specific farm. The farmer picks a country and city (all Pakistan cities are listed; any other place can be typed), chooses or types their current crops, and gives soil type, water supply and priorities (save water, healthier soil, income, safety from heat and cold). Results appear only after every answer is given: a best match, a comparison with the current rotation, a season calendar, 20-year climate trends and, for Pakistan, a NASA satellite view of rainfall and soil water.

HOW IT WORKS

1. NASA POWER monthly data (temperature, rain, root-zone soil wetness, 2005-2024) is fetched live for the farm's location.

2. We estimate crop water use (Hargreaves evapotranspiration with crop coefficients) and find climate-suitable sowing windows for each crop.

3. Every two-crop rotation is scored 0-10 for water use, soil health, income and weather safety, weighted by the farmer's priorities. Rotations that need too much irrigation for rain-fed farms, repeat the same plant family, or leave soil bare in heavy-rain months are penalized.

4. Results are explained in plain words with benefits, risks and what the tool does not know. Farmers can listen to the summary, copy it or save the plan as a PDF.

5. For Pakistan, NASA GPM IMERG rainfall and GLDAS root-zone soil moisture (via NASA Giovanni, 2005-2025) show monsoon strength, extreme-rain years and dry months.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Helps farmers use less irrigation water, protect soil with cover and nitrogen-fixing crops, and avoid heat, cold and flood risk. It is free, mobile friendly, supports 100 languages (6 built in; others translated on demand when a server key is available), accepts any crop typed by the farmer, and tells farmers to confirm results with a local agriculture officer.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a fixed crop list, the tool builds sowing windows from each place's own NASA climate, so it works anywhere. The farmer's own priorities change the ranking, and the tool is open about its limits.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no framework); Python standard library for data download and conversion; NASA POWER API; NASA Giovanni; Open-Meteo geocoding; GitHub Pages hosting.

SI ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

Claude (Anthropic) helped write the code, interface text, translations and this description. The scoring design, dataset choice, data downloads and testing were directed by the team. Translations other than English are AI-generated and not yet reviewed by native speakers.
